title: Characterization, release kinetics, and application of sodium alginate active packaging incorporated with eugenol‐loaded shellac/gum arabic nanoparticles for chilled pork preservation
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Hydrophobic, volatile eugenol may disperse poorly and release rapidly from hydrophilic sodium alginate (SA) films. This study incorporated eugenol-loaded shellac/gum arabic complex nanoparticles (SGAE NPs) into SA films and evaluated film properties, eugenol release, antibacterial activity, and chilled pork preservation.

RESULTS

Gum arabic concentration affected nanoparticle characteristics. SGAE3 provided the highest encapsulation efficiency (72.7%), while SGAE5 had the highest numerical loading capacity (36 g kg−1). Incorporating SGAE NPs reduced film water solubility from 445 to 226–275 g kg−1 and increased tensile strength from 5.3 to 21.9 MPa. After 48 h, cumulative eugenol release from the nanocomposite films remained below 65% in water and 55% in 950 mL L−1 ethanol, compared with 93.5% and 78.9%, respectively, from the free-eugenol control. Korsmeyer–Peppas fitting showed formulation- and simulant-dependent release behavior, with anomalous transport characteristics limited to selected formulations. The films inhibited Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus in vitro. In pork stored at 4 °C, the SGAE-containing films retarded increases in total viable count and total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N). The first measured exceedance of the 150 mg kg−1 TVB-N limit was delayed from day 4 in the unwrapped control to day 8 in the SGAE film groups.

CONCLUSION

SGAE NPs improved selected functional properties of SA films and sustained eugenol release. These films show potential for chilled pork packaging, although long-term stability, lipid oxidation, sensory quality, and sealed-packaging performance require further evaluation. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
